title: What an agent can do with Talonic
seoTitle: Talonic MCP Server: What Your AI Agent Can Do — Talonic
description: Connect Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client to Talonic. Your agent finds documents, extracts fields, answers cited questions and runs processes.

content.text: The Talonic MCP server lets an AI agent work with the documents and data in your Talonic workspace the way you would in the web app: find a document, pull fields out of it, ask a question across everything, run a Spec, sign off a step, or set up a process. It is for anyone who wants their agent (in Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Cowork or their own) to do document work for them.
New here? [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install) in two minutes, then try the [contract question recipe](/docs/mcp/recipes/answer-a-contract-question).

items: **Find.** Locate documents by name or keyword, filter them by extracted values ("invoices over 10,000 EUR"), and find which field holds a concept. [Find tools](/docs/mcp/tools).

**Read and extract.** Turn any PDF, scan, image, DOCX or email into JSON that matches the fields you ask for, with a confidence score per field and the page and passage each value came from. Or get the full text.
**Ask.** Ask a question in plain words and get an answer with citations to the documents it rests on, checked before it is returned.
**Run.** Run one of your workspace's Specs over a set of documents and read back one clean row per document.
**Review and decide.** Sign off or send back items waiting for you, and take on checks or decisions your workspace hands to an outside agent.
**Build and automate.** Describe a process in your own words (what comes in, what is checked, who signs, what goes out), test it on real documents, publish it, and watch its runs.
**Look after the workspace.** Keep each company's documents apart, check credits, pricing and usage.

content.text: Your agent calls Talonic tools; Talonic does the reading and checking and returns structured results. Every call runs as you: it sees only your workspace and can do only what your role allows, exactly like the web app. Writes that send mail, call other systems or can't be undone say so in their description, and the agent is told to call them only when you ask.

items: **40 tools** are listed in every session.
**21 process tools** are listed when your role can see processes in the workspace.
Apps you have enabled (for example Contracts or Accounts Payable) add their own tools to sessions that can use them; see [Apps](https://talonic.com/docs/apps).
**Hosted** at `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`. Sign in with your Talonic account; no key to copy. Best for Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code.
**Local** with `npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest` and an API key. Best for desktop and IDE clients that start the server on your machine and can read local files.

content.text: Once connected, ask your agent: "What documents do I have in Talonic about invoices?" It calls [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) and lists them. Then: "Extract the vendor, total and due date from the first one." It calls [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) and returns JSON with a confidence score for each field.

items: [Connect your client](/docs/mcp/install)
[Tools by task](/docs/mcp/tools)
[Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files)
[Recipe: set up a workspace end to end](/docs/mcp/recipes/set-up-a-workspace)

faq.question: Which AI clients work with the Talonic MCP server?
faq.answer: Any client that speaks the Model Context Protocol. Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue and Cowork have step-by-step instructions on the Connect page.

faq.question: Can the agent see other people's documents?
faq.answer: No. Every call runs with your credential and your workspace role, so the agent sees and changes exactly what you could in the web app, and nothing else.

faq.question: Does using the MCP server cost extra?
faq.answer: No. Tool calls use the same credits as the web app and the API. Reading, listing and searching are free; extracting, asking and running Specs use credits. Each tool page says what it costs.

title: Why connect your agent to Talonic
seoTitle: Why Connect Your AI Agent to Talonic Over MCP — Talonic
description: Reading documents inside a chat gives you text. Connecting Talonic gives your agent checked fields, cited answers, your saved Specs and processes it can run.

content.text: An agent can read a PDF you paste into a chat. What it can't do on its own is give you the same fields every time, show where each value came from, remember the thousand documents you processed last quarter, or start the approval your team runs on every invoice. Connecting Talonic adds those.

items: **Same fields, every time.** You say which fields you want once (or save them); every document comes back in that shape, with a confidence score per field.
**Evidence.** Each value links to the page and passage it came from, and answers cite the documents they rest on, so you can check before you act.
**Your whole workspace.** Questions run across every document you have added, not only the one in the chat.
**Your rules.** The agent runs the Specs and processes your team already set up, with the same permissions and sign-offs as the web app.
**Large files.** Files too big for a chat go through an upload link instead.

content.text: Start with [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install), or see [what an agent can do](/docs/mcp).

title: Get an API key
seoTitle: Get a Talonic API Key for the MCP Server — Talonic Docs
description: Create a Talonic API key for local MCP installs and header-based clients. Hosted connectors in Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code sign you in without a key.

content.text: A local install (`npx @talonic/mcp`) and clients that send their own headers need an API key. Hosted connectors in Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code sign you in with your Talonic account instead, so you can skip this page for those.

items: Sign in at [app.talonic.com](https://app.talonic.com).
Open **Settings → API Keys** and choose **Create key**.
Copy the key. It starts with `tlnc_` and is shown once.
Put it in your client's config as `TALONIC_API_KEY` (local) or an `Authorization: Bearer` header (hosted). [Connect your agent](/docs/mcp/install) has the snippets.

content.text: A key acts as the person who created it, in one workspace, and never with more rights than that person's role. Create a separate key per workspace and per machine so you can revoke one without breaking the others.
Keep keys out of source control and screenshots. If a key leaks, revoke it under **Settings → API Keys** and create a new one.

faq.question: Do I need an API key to use Talonic in Claude.ai or ChatGPT?
faq.answer: No. Hosted connectors sign you in with your Talonic account and keep the access token for you. You only need a key for a local install or a client that sends its own headers.

title: Connect your agent
seoTitle: Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor to Talonic MCP — Talonic
description: Connect Talonic to Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue or Cowork: hosted with sign-in, or local with npx and an API key.

content.text: Connect Talonic to your AI client and your agent can work with your workspace. Pick your client below; most take under two minutes.

items: **Hosted** (`https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`): nothing to install, always the latest version, and you sign in with your Talonic account (OAuth). Files reach Talonic by URL, by document id or through an [upload link](/docs/mcp/files).

**Local** (`npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest`, Node.js 18 or later): needs an [API key](/docs/mcp/api-key). The agent can pass files on your machine by path. Pin an exact version (for example `@talonic/mcp@0.1.100`) for repeatable setups.

content.text: Both list the same tools and work on the same workspace. Signing in grants `extract:write`, `documents:read`, `schemas:read` and `apps:decide`; you can revoke access by removing the connector or the key.
Add Talonic once as a connector; it then works in Claude.ai and the Claude Desktop app.

items: Open **Settings → Connectors** in [claude.ai](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors) or Claude Desktop and choose **Add custom connector**.
Enter the URL `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`. No headers, no key.
Choose **Connect**, sign in to Talonic and approve access. If you belong to several workspaces, pick one.
Start a new conversation. The Talonic tools are available.

content.text: To run the server on your own machine instead (so the agent can read local files by path), add the local config to `claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/`, Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\`) and quit and reopen Claude Desktop:

items: In ChatGPT, open **Settings → Apps**.
Find **Talonic** and choose **Connect**.
Sign in to Talonic and approve access.
In a new chat, ask for Talonic by name the first time ("Use Talonic to find my latest invoice").

content.text: ChatGPT lists every tool except the two generic data-query tools; ask questions with [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) there. Results show as cards in the chat.
Hosted, signed in with your Talonic account:

content.code:
claude mcp add --transport http talonic https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp
# then run /mcp inside Claude Code and choose Authenticate
claude mcp add talonic --env TALONIC_API_KEY=tlnc_your_key_here -- npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest

content.text: Open **Cursor Settings → MCP → Add new MCP server**, or edit `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Use the local config to let the agent read files in your project by path:
Save and reload the window. The `talonic` entry turns green and lists its tools.
In VS Code, open the Cline panel → **MCP Servers → Configure** and add one of these, then restart the panel:
Cline can auto-approve tools. Approving the read-only ones (search, look-ups, listings) lets it explore without asking; keep writes on manual approval.
Edit `~/.continue/config.json` (shared by VS Code and JetBrains) and add an entry to `mcpServers`, then reload the IDE window:
Open **Settings → MCP Servers → Add**, paste one of these and restart Cowork:
Cowork shows your saved schemas under resources (`talonic://schemas`), so you can pick one before extracting.

Point a client that supports remote servers at `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp` (it will start a Talonic sign-in, or send `Authorization: Bearer tlnc_…`), or have it start `npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest` with `TALONIC_API_KEY` set. [Configuration](/docs/mcp/configuration) lists every setting.

Ask your agent: "List my Talonic schemas." It calls [`talonic_list_schemas`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-schemas), which is free and changes nothing. A list (or an empty list in a new workspace) means you are connected. An authentication error means the key or sign-in is wrong; see [Troubleshooting](/docs/mcp/troubleshooting).

faq.question: Should I use the hosted server or the local one?
faq.answer: Use hosted for Claude.ai, ChatGPT and Claude Code: you sign in and there is nothing to install. Use local in desktop and IDE clients when you want the agent to pass files from your machine by path.

faq.question: Do the hosted and local servers offer the same tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The only difference is that a local install can read files on your machine by path; hosted sessions use a URL, a document id or an upload link.

faq.question: How do I disconnect?
faq.answer: Remove the connector in your client, or revoke the API key under Settings → API Keys in the Talonic web app.

description: Create a new app. It starts disabled with no versions; the slug can no longer change once a version is published. Part of the Talonic MCP tools for building…

content.text: Create a new app. It starts disabled with no versions; the slug can no longer change once a version is published. Listed only when the credential can read the workspace's apps. The platform checks the caller's role, per-app access and key scopes on every call.

items: USE WHEN: the user asks to set up a new app. ARGS: slug (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, 3-64 chars), display_name, mode, optional one-sentence description.

Modes: rules (decides from written rules), assisted (rules with people confirming), external (an outside agent decides through the decision-task tools), autonomous (finds candidate rules in the app's data).
RETURNS: the manifest; use its `id` (UUID) with every other app tool.

FLOW: talonic_create_app -> talonic_save_app_draft -> talonic_interpret_app_rules -> talonic_publish_app -> talonic_run_app (dry_run first) -> talonic_get_app_run / talonic_get_run_verdicts -> talonic_save_app_acceptance + talonic_check_app_acceptance -> talonic_enable_app.

params.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3-64 chars.

title: Tools by task
seoTitle: Talonic MCP Tools by Task: Find, Extract, Ask, Run — Talonic
description: Every Talonic MCP tool grouped by the job: find documents, extract fields, ask cited questions, run Specs, review, build and run processes, check credits.

content.text: Pick the job, then the tool. Your agent reads the same descriptions and usually chooses well on its own; this page is for you to see what is possible and to steer it.

Rule of thumb: a question about what documents say goes to [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask); a named file goes through [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) first; fields from one document come from [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract).

Start here when the user names a document, a value or a concept. [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) turns a file name or keyword into a `document_id`; [`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter) finds documents by an extracted value; [`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data) finds which field holds a concept.

items: [`talonic_get_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-document): Fetch a single document's metadata and processing status from the workspace.
[`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search): Find documents, fields, schemas, or sources in the workspace.
[`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter): Find documents by their extracted field VALUES using composable conditions (e.g. 'invoices where total > 1000').

[`talonic_list_fields`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-fields): List the fields your workspace's documents carry (vendor name, invoice total, notice period …), each with a stable id, how established it is (maturity), data type, synonyms and how often it occurs.

[`talonic_get_field`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-field): Describe one field: what it means, its synonyms and other names, maturity, where it occurs (document and occurrence counts, first and last seen, which document types), its values (top values with counts, distinct count, examples), which schemas use it, and the fields merged into it (superseded_by).

[`talonic_field_values`](/docs/mcp/tools/field-values): Read a field's CURRENT VALUES across documents, with evidence: one row per value, with the document id, filename and type, the value, its confidence, the label it appeared under in the document, the exact source text, and how the label was matched to this field (`resolved_by`).

[`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data): Find where the data behind a concept lives before querying anything: turns a phrase ('payment volume per transaction', 'counterparty', 'Vertragslaufzeit') into the fields, values, documents and text passages that carry it, matching what it means as well as its words, even when the field has a different name.

content.text: Get fields as JSON with [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract), or the full text with [`talonic_to_markdown`](/docs/mcp/tools/to-markdown). Save field sets you reuse; hand the user an upload link when a file can't be passed directly ([Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files)).

items: [`talonic_list_schemas`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-schemas): List the saved schemas in the workspace as compact summaries (id, short_id, name, description, version, field_count).
[`talonic_get_schema`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-schema): Get one saved schema with its full field definition (field names, types, descriptions).
[`talonic_save_schema`](/docs/mcp/tools/save-schema): Save a reusable schema to the workspace for use across future extractions.
[`talonic_to_markdown`](/docs/mcp/tools/to-markdown): Get the full text of a document as markdown, including scanned pages.
[`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract): Extract structured, schema-validated JSON from a document: PDF, scan, image, DOCX, email, or photo.
[`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload): Get a browser upload link the user opens to add a file to their workspace.

content.text: For any question about what the documents say (totals, duplicates, comparisons, a clause), call [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) first: one call returns a cited, checked answer.

items: [`talonic_list_agent_tools`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-agent-tools): List Talonic's data tools: read-only look-ups and queries over the workspace (find_data, describe_data, query_data for a read-only SQL query over the extracted data, get_document_markdown, workspace_overview, …), each with its input schema and whether THIS credential may call it.

[`talonic_invoke_agent_tool`](/docs/mcp/tools/invoke-agent-tool): Run ONE named data tool directly and get its exact output (e.g. `query_data` for a read-only SQL SELECT over the extracted data, `describe_data` for the queryable field list, `get_document_markdown` to read a document's text).
[`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask): Ask a natural-language question over the workspace's documents and get a cited, verified answer (markdown).
[`talonic_get_answer`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-answer): Poll an ask started by talonic_ask that was still processing when the wait ended.

content.text: A Spec is a saved set of fields and checks your team set up in Talonic. Run it over documents to get one clean row per document.

items: [`talonic_list_specs`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-specs): List the workspace's Specs.

[`talonic_get_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-spec): Get one Spec's structure: identity and version state, the schema its output rows follow, `nodes[]` (the steps as the user set them up, in editing order), `phases[]` (the same steps in the order a run carries them out; one check can appear more than once, so the two lists can differ), and `fields[]` (Spec field ↔ schema field).
[`talonic_run_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/run-spec): Run one of the workspace's Specs over documents, in one call, and get one structured row per document.
[`talonic_get_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-run): Poll a Spec run started by talonic_run_spec: normalised status plus progress per document and, for run_kind 'pipeline', per step.

[`talonic_get_run_results`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-run-results): Read a Spec run's structured rows — one row per document with the Spec's fields as clean values (values held for review come back null), plus the column definitions.

content.text: Work that waits for a person or an outside agent: sign-offs and forms waiting for the user, checks a Spec hands to your agent, and decisions an app hands out. [Run Talonic tasks from your own agent](/docs/mcp/run-talonic-tasks) explains the claim, work, submit loop.

items: [`talonic_list_agent_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-agent-tasks): List the agent tasks waiting in this workspace: checks a Spec hands to an outside agent (your agent) instead of a person, one per document.
[`talonic_get_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-agent-task): Read one agent task: its fixed input, instructions, and the output fields it expects.
[`talonic_claim_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-agent-task): Claim an available agent task so no one else works on it, or reclaim it after its lease expires.
[`talonic_heartbeat_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-agent-task): Extend the lease on a claimed agent task so you keep it while you work.
[`talonic_submit_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-agent-task): Submit the output fields for a claimed agent task; the document then continues through its Spec.
[`talonic_list_decision_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-decision-tasks): List one External-mode app's decision tasks (runs waiting for an outside agent to decide), newest first.

[`talonic_claim_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-decision-task): Claim an available decision task (or reclaim one whose lease expired) and receive the decision bundle: task metadata with the new execution_epoch, output_contract, precedents, and a package descriptor { package_kind, record_count, page_size, first_cursor, documents }.

[`talonic_read_decision_package`](/docs/mcp/tools/read-decision-package): Read one page of a claimed decision task's fixed input: the records the decision must be made from, each with the locator to cite as evidence.
[`talonic_heartbeat_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-decision-task): Extend the lease on a claimed decision task, never past its sla_deadline_at.
[`talonic_submit_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-decision-task): Submit the decision for a claimed decision task; Talonic checks it before saving anything, then the run continues.
[`talonic_release_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/release-decision-task): Release a claimed decision task back to 'available' without deciding it; the next claim bumps the epoch.

[`talonic_fail_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/fail-decision-task): Report that the claimed decision task cannot be decided: sends it to a person for review with your reason AND applies the app's declared fallback policy (rules decide, hold for review, or fail the run).
[`talonic_process_waiting_for_me`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-waiting-for-me): Sign-offs and forms waiting for the caller (the person behind the key): per process and step, how many items wait.
[`talonic_process_sign`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-sign): Sign a sign-off step of a run for the caller: approve all waiting items, or only `items`.
[`talonic_process_send_back`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-send-back): Send items back from a sign-off step with a reason, for the caller: the opposite of talonic_process_sign.

content.text: Describe a process in plain words, check it, test it on real documents in a test copy, then publish it. Nothing runs for real until [`talonic_process_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-publish). Process tools are listed when your role can see processes.

items: [`talonic_process_get`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-get): One process with its draft: fields, steps (id, kind, name, settings) and the arrows between them.
[`talonic_process_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-create): Set up a new process as a DRAFT.
[`talonic_process_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-change): Change a process draft from an instruction in plain words: add, remove or reorder steps, change who decides, what is sent, any setting.

[`talonic_process_check`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-check): What a draft still needs before it can go live (`stillNeeded`, per step), every problem the check finds, and what publishing would change against the live version.
[`talonic_process_test_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-test-run): Run the DRAFT on real documents in a test copy: nothing is delivered, emailed or called.
[`talonic_process_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-publish): Make the draft the LIVE version.
[`talonic_process_versions`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-versions): The published versions of a process, newest first, with who published and why.
[`talonic_process_rollback`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-rollback): Make an earlier published version live again.
[`talonic_process_delete`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-delete): Delete a process.

[`talonic_process_setup`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-setup): What processes of this workspace can use: who a step can wait for (roles, groups), the connected mailboxes and whether each may send, the names of stored secrets (never values), and the shared data a look-up step can read.

[`talonic_process_mailbox_ownership`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-mailbox-ownership): Say whether a connected mailbox is one person's own (`individual`: only that person may put it on a process) or the company's (`company`: everyone who builds processes may).
[`talonic_process_address`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-address): The address other systems send items to (a webhook).

content.text: Start a published process for one item, see where its runs stand, follow one item through every step, and retry failed steps once the cause is fixed.

items: [`talonic_process_list`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-list): List the workspace's processes: name, live version (null = draft only), folder, tags and number of steps.
[`talonic_process_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-run): Start a published process for one item with values by field name, e.g. {"Vendor": "Acme", "Amount": 1200}.
[`talonic_process_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-status): Where a process run stands: per step, how many items are waiting, done or failed, and each item's state.
[`talonic_process_runs`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-runs): Runs across all processes, newest first: state (running, completed, failed, stuck = open with a failed item), items done, waiting and failed.
[`talonic_process_item`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-item): One item's way through a run, step by step (status, time, note such as why it stopped or where a mail went), and its values now.
[`talonic_process_retry`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-retry): Try every failed step of a run again.

content.text: See which Talonic apps the workspace has. Apps you have enabled (for example Contracts, Accounts Payable, Document Generation or Price Baseline) add their own tools to sessions that can use them; each app's page under [Apps](https://talonic.com/docs/apps) lists them.

items: [`talonic_list_apps`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-apps): List the Talonic Apps in the user's workspace: id, slug, name, one-line description, mode and whether each is enabled.

content.text: Keep each company's documents apart with accounts, and check balance, pricing and what credits went on.

items: [`talonic_get_balance`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-balance): Read the workspace's Talonic credit balance, EUR value, tier, 30-day burn, and projected runway.
[`talonic_get_pricing`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-pricing): Read Talonic's machine-readable credit pricing catalog: fixed per-unit rates so you can predict spend BEFORE running anything.
[`talonic_get_usage`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-usage): Read the workspace's per-function credit consumption over a trailing window: where the credits actually went.
[`talonic_list_accounts`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-accounts): List the workspace's accounts: the companies (portfolio companies, clients, entities) whose documents it keeps apart.
[`talonic_create_account`](/docs/mcp/tools/create-account): Create an account: a company whose documents the workspace keeps apart, so answers about it never mix in another company's files.

faq.question: Why does my agent not list some of these tools?
faq.answer: Process tools appear only when your role can see processes, app tools only when the app is enabled for you, and ChatGPT omits the two generic data-query tools. Everything else is listed in every session.

faq.question: How do I list schemas via MCP?
faq.answer: Call talonic_list_schemas to get all saved schemas with their definitions. The talonic://schemas resource also exposes this data.

faq.question: What is the difference between the UUID and SCH-XXXXXXXX ID?
faq.answer: Both reference the same schema. The UUID (id) is the full identifier, while SCH-XXXXXXXX (short_id) is a shorter, human-friendly format. Either can be passed as schema_id to talonic_extract.

faq.question: Does talonic_list_schemas require any parameters?
faq.answer: No. It takes no input parameters and returns all saved schemas in the workspace with their full definitions.

faq.question: Is talonic_list_schemas free to call?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads metadata only and uses no credits, so an agent can call it whenever it needs to check for an existing schema.

faq.question: How do I know which schema to use for a document?
faq.answer: Match the schema's name and description to the document. For example, use a 'Standard Invoice' schema for invoices and a 'Certificate of Insurance' schema for COIs. When unsure, start with an inline schema and save it once the results look right.

faq.question: How do I save a schema via MCP?
faq.answer: Call talonic_save_schema with a name and JSON Schema definition. It returns a schema_id for reuse in talonic_extract calls.

faq.question: When should I save a schema vs use an inline schema?
faq.answer: Save a schema when you will reuse it across many documents (e.g., a standard invoice template). Use inline schemas for one-off extractions or when iterating on schema design with the user.

faq.question: Can I update a saved schema?
faq.answer: Schema updates are managed through the Talonic dashboard. The version field in the response tracks changes. Via MCP, you can save a new schema with a different name if the design changes significantly.

faq.question: What is the recommended workflow for schema design?
faq.answer: Iterate inline first: pass the schema directly to talonic_extract, review results with the user, adjust fields as needed. Once the user confirms the schema produces good results, call talonic_save_schema to persist it. This prevents cluttering the workspace with draft schemas that never get used.

faq.question: Should I include a description when saving a schema?
faq.answer: Yes. A clear description ('Vendor, line items, totals and payment terms from invoices') helps people on your team and agents pick the right schema for a document.

title: talonic_get_document
seoTitle: talonic_get_document — Document Metadata & Status Tool
description: MCP tool that fetches one document's details by id: status, page count, type, language and a link to open it in Talonic. Use it to follow an upload too.

content.text: Fetch a single document's metadata and processing status from the workspace.

items: **Use it when:** 'tell me about document X', or to poll status after talonic_request_upload until the file is ready.
**Not for:** full text (use talonic_to_markdown) · extracted fields (use talonic_extract).
**By file name:** if the user names a file, call talonic_search first to get its document_id, then call this.
**Arguments:** document_id.

**Returns:** filename, pages, type_detected, language, and `status`. Status lifecycle: pending_upload -> uploading -> queued -> extracting -> completed. Wait for `completed` before calling talonic_extract on a freshly uploaded doc. Terminal failure statuses: ocr_failed, extraction_failed, error — stop polling and report the failure to the user if any of these appear. To read the document's text, call talonic_to_markdown with this id.

content.text: Listed in every Talonic MCP session, local or hosted.

items: **Reads only.** It never changes workspace data.
**Cost:** no credits.

faq.question: How do I get document metadata via MCP?
faq.answer: Call talonic_get_document with the document id. It returns the file name, status, pages, detected type, language and links.

faq.question: Does talonic_get_document return extracted data?
faq.answer: No. It returns metadata (filename, status, pages, type, language, links). For extracted field data, use talonic_extract with the same document_id.

faq.question: How can I link the user to the original document?
faq.answer: The response includes links.dashboard, which is a direct URL to view the document in the Talonic web interface. Present this to the user when they need to verify an extraction.

faq.question: Does talonic_get_document cost any credits?
faq.answer: No. It is a free look-up. Call it as often as needed to check status or get the link to the document.

faq.question: What document statuses can talonic_get_document return?
faq.answer: While a file is on its way: pending_upload, uploading, queued, extracting, then completed (or extracted for text-only uploads). ocr_failed, extraction_failed and error are final: stop and tell the user.

title: talonic_search

faq.question: What does talonic_search do?
faq.answer: It finds documents, fields, schemas and sources whose name or text contains your keyword, and returns their ids. Search with one short, singular word or an exact file name.

faq.question: When should I use talonic_search vs talonic_filter?
faq.answer: Use search to find a document or field by name ('Acme', 'invoice'). Use filter for conditions on extracted values ('invoices over 1000 EUR').

faq.question: Can I search for schemas by name?
faq.answer: Yes. talonic_search includes schemas in its results. If you search for 'invoice', any schema with 'invoice' in its name or description will appear in the schemas array of the response. This is useful for discovering existing templates before creating new ones.

faq.answer: The fields in the response carry a canonicalName and a filterable flag. Use canonicalName values where filterable is true as `field` in talonic_filter conditions.

title: talonic_filter
seoTitle: talonic_filter — Filter Documents by Extracted Fields
description: MCP tool that finds documents by their extracted field values with conditions such as eq, gt, between and contains, and reports fields it couldn't match.

content.text: Find documents by their extracted field VALUES using composable conditions (e.g. 'invoices where total > 1000').

items: **Use it when:** value-based criteria on extracted fields — numeric/date/text comparisons or presence checks.
**Not for:** free-text / concept search (use talonic_search) · a single document by id (use talonic_get_document).

**Arguments:** conditions[] (AND-ed). Each = EXACTLY ONE of `field` (canonical name) or `field_id` (UUID), an `operator`, and usually a `value`. Operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between (needs `value` AND `value_to`), contains, is_empty / is_not_empty (no value). `value`/`value_to` are string|number|boolean matching the field type (ISO YYYY-MM-DD for dates).

**Text filters:** for eq/contains/is_not_empty on a text field, just TRY a natural field name ('currency', 'vendor_name') — names resolve server-side and an unresolved field surfaces in warnings[] rather than erroring. Do NOT block on discovering the field first; search-first is only required for numeric operators.

**Numeric guard:** gt/gte/lt/lte/between only work when the field's dataType is 'number'. Call talonic_search first and check dataType; a numeric op on a string field returns zero matches. If the response has `warnings[]`, surface them to the user — do not silently retry.
**Returns:** data[] (matching documents with field values), total, warnings[].

content.text: Listed in every Talonic MCP session, local or hosted.

items: **Reads only.** It never changes workspace data.
**Cost:** no credits.

faq.question: How do I filter documents by field value?
faq.answer: Use talonic_filter with field names and operators such as eq, gt, between or contains. Field names are matched for you; one it can't match comes back in warnings[].

faq.question: How do I find the correct canonical field names for filtering?
faq.answer: For text fields, try the natural name ('vendor_name', 'currency'). For numbers and dates, call talonic_search first: the canonical names are in fields[].canonicalName.

faq.question: Can I combine free-text search with field filters?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass `search` alongside `conditions` to combine a keyword with value conditions in one call.

faq.question: What operators are available for talonic_filter?
faq.answer: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between (with value_to), contains, is_empty and is_not_empty. The number comparisons work only on fields stored as numbers.

faq.question: Why does my filter return zero results even though matching documents exist?
faq.answer: Usually a number comparison on a field stored as text, for example amounts with currency symbols. Check the field's dataType first, and read warnings[] on the response.

faq.answer: Each talonic_extract response carries a cost field with the credits it used. Check the balance before a large batch and again after it.

description: MCP tool that gives the user a browser link to upload a file too large for a chat tool call. Returns the link, a reserved document_id and when the link expires.

After the user uploads, poll talonic_get_document on that document_id until status is 'completed' (or 'extracted' when add_to_workspace is false), then call talonic_extract if you need fields. If status becomes ocr_failed, extraction_failed, or error, stop polling and report the failure to the user.

faq.answer: In Claude.ai and ChatGPT, where a tool call can carry only about 32 KB; real documents are larger and arrive cut short as file_data. Local installs (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, Cowork) can pass files by path instead.

faq.question: Does a user message like 'uploaded' mean the file is ready to extract?
faq.answer: No. It means the browser finished sending the file; Talonic still needs a short while to read it. Check talonic_get_document until status is 'completed' before extracting.

faq.question: What happens if the user never opens the upload link?
faq.answer: The reserved document stays in pending_upload. The link stops working at expires_at; ask for a new one with talonic_request_upload, which reserves a new document_id.

faq.question: Can the agent PUT the file to the upload_url itself?
faq.answer: Usually not: hosted chat clients can't send data to arbitrary addresses. And the user should choose the file anyway, so give them the link.

faq.question: How do I keep a company's files together, and make them workspace data?
faq.answer: Pass `account` (a company name, alias or id from talonic_list_accounts; create one with talonic_create_account) so the document belongs to that company, and `add_to_workspace: true` so it is fully processed and can be asked about later. Without add_to_workspace only its text is kept, for one talonic_extract call.

faq.question: Why a separate tool instead of changing `talonic_extract`?
faq.answer: Keeping the upload step separate means the user sees the link and knows what is happening, and talonic_extract behaves the same for every file.

description: MCP tool that releases a claimed decision task back to available without deciding it, so another agent can claim it; the next claim bumps the execution epoch.

content.text: Release a claimed decision task back to 'available' without deciding it; the next claim bumps the epoch.

items: **Use it when:** you cannot finish within the lease or SLA but another claimant could decide it.
**Not for:** declaring the task undecidable (talonic_fail_decision_task, which raises a review and applies the app's fallback) or keeping the lease (talonic_heartbeat_decision_task).
**Arguments:** task_id and execution_epoch. Stale epoch is HTTP 409.

**Access:** a tlnc_ key needs a per-app 'decide' grant; an OAuth connector session needs the apps:decide scope (consented at connect) and a live workspace role of senior_member or above. A 403 (decide_grant_required, insufficient_scope, insufficient_tier) names what is missing — tell the user, do not retry.

content.text: Listed in every session. Calling it needs a per-app `decide` grant on an API key, or, on a connector session, the `apps:decide` scope and a workspace role of senior member or above. Without it the tool stays listed but is marked not callable, and the agent can tell you to reconnect.

items: **Not read-only.** It can add to or change workspace data.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Decision task UUID.

params.name: execution_epoch
params.description: Execution epoch returned by the successful claim. Stale epochs are rejected with 409. Range: 1 to 2147483647.

content.text: A failed call comes back as a tool error with the HTTP status and a message that says what to change. [Troubleshooting](/docs/mcp/troubleshooting) lists the common ones.

faq.question: Release or fail — which one?
faq.answer: Release when the task is decidable but not by you right now: another claimant gets the same package and contract. Fail when no claimant could decide it from this package: that raises a Human Review with your reason and applies the app's fallback policy.

title: talonic_fail_decision_task
seoTitle: talonic_fail_decision_task — Declare a Task Undecidable
description: MCP tool that marks a claimed decision task as undecidable: it raises a Human Review carrying the agent's reason and applies the app's declared fallback policy.

content.text: Report that the claimed decision task cannot be decided: sends it to a person for review with your reason AND applies the app's declared fallback policy (rules decide, hold for review, or fail the run).

items: **Use it when:** the package is insufficient or contradictory and no claimant could decide it. This ends the task (status 'failed').
**Not for:** temporary give-backs (talonic_release_decision_task) or a decision you can make with low confidence (submit it with confidence set).
**Arguments:** task_id, execution_epoch, reason (up to 2,000 characters). Stale epoch is HTTP 409.

**Access:** a tlnc_ key needs a per-app 'decide' grant; an OAuth connector session needs the apps:decide scope (consented at connect) and a live workspace role of senior_member or above. A 403 (decide_grant_required, insufficient_scope, insufficient_tier) names what is missing — tell the user, do not retry.

content.text: Listed in every session. Calling it needs a per-app `decide` grant on an API key, or, on a connector session, the `apps:decide` scope and a workspace role of senior member or above. Without it the tool stays listed but is marked not callable, and the agent can tell you to reconnect.

items: **Changes workspace data and can't be undone.** Call it only when the user asked.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Decision task UUID.

params.name: execution_epoch
params.description: Execution epoch returned by the successful claim. Stale epochs are rejected with 409. Range: 1 to 2147483647.

params.name: reason
params.description: Why the task cannot be decided, up to 2,000 characters. Recorded on the Human Review the fail raises.

content.text: A failed call comes back as a tool error with the HTTP status and a message that says what to change. [Troubleshooting](/docs/mcp/troubleshooting) lists the common ones.

faq.question: Is failing a decision task destructive?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is marked destructive. No data is deleted, but the task ends as failed, a review is raised with your reason, and the app's fallback runs, which can fail the whole run. A failed task can't be claimed again.

content.text: Before Talonic can read a document, the file has to reach it. This page shows the four ways an agent can do that, which one to use, and what to tell the user while a file is on its way.

items: **Already in the workspace.** Use its `document_id`. If the user names the file, find the id with [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) (search by file name or one keyword). Free and instant.
**On a public URL.** Pass `file_url` (https). Talonic fetches it. Good for links the user pastes.
**On the user's machine, in a local install.** Pass `file_path`; the local server reads the file. Small files can also go as `file_data` (base64) with `filename`.
**Anything else, especially in Claude.ai or ChatGPT.** Call [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) and give the user the link. They open it in their browser and drop the file.

content.text: Hosted chat clients cap the size of a tool call (around 32 KB), which is smaller than most real documents. A file sent as `file_data` there arrives cut short and comes back with empty fields. Use an upload link instead.
The upload link, step by step

items: The agent calls [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) with the `filename`. Pass `account` to file it under one company, and `add_to_workspace: true` if the user will ask questions about it later (otherwise only its text is kept for the next extraction).
It returns `upload_url`, a `document_id` reserved for the file, and `expires_at`. The agent shows the user the link and says when it expires.
The user opens the link and drops the file. The agent checks [`talonic_get_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-document) every few seconds.
When `status` is `completed` (or `extracted` without `add_to_workspace`), the file is ready: extract fields, read its text, or ask about it.

content.title: Status while a file is on its way

params.name: pending_upload
params.description: Link issued; the user has not dropped the file yet.

params.name: uploading
params.description: The file is arriving. Keep checking.

params.name: queued / extracting
params.description: Talonic is reading the file.

params.name: extracted
params.description: Text is ready (uploads without `add_to_workspace`).

params.name: completed
params.description: Fully processed and searchable.

params.name: ocr_failed / extraction_failed / error
params.description: Stop checking and tell the user; the file could not be read. A clearer scan or the original file usually works.

content.text: PDFs (text or scanned), images and phone photos, Word documents (DOCX) and emails. Long documents take longer; very large files are better sent as an upload link or a URL than as bytes.

If the workspace holds documents for several companies (clients, portfolio companies, entities), pass `account` when uploading. Questions scoped to that account never mix in another company's files. [`talonic_list_accounts`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-accounts) lists them; [`talonic_create_account`](/docs/mcp/tools/create-account) adds one.
Issuing a link and checking status are free. Reading a new file uses credits, as in the web app; [`talonic_get_pricing`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-pricing) shows the rates.

faq.question: Why does my agent ask me to open a link instead of reading the file I attached?
faq.answer: Hosted chat clients limit how much data one tool call can carry, so an attached document would arrive incomplete. The upload link sends the whole file straight from your browser to your workspace.

faq.question: How long is an upload link valid?
faq.answer: Until the `expires_at` time returned with it. If it expires, ask the agent for a new link; nothing is lost.

seoTitle: Drag and Drop Files into Your Agent: Talonic MCP Docs
description: Drop a file into your AI client and have Talonic read it: when attaching works, when an upload link is better, and how a local install reads files by path.

content.text: Desktop and IDE clients running the local server can pass a dropped or attached file straight to Talonic. In Claude.ai and ChatGPT, attached files are too large for a tool call, so the agent gives you an upload link instead.
All the options, and which to use when, are on [Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files).

title: How a file gets to Talonic
seoTitle: How a File Gets from Your Agent to Talonic MCP — Talonic
description: What happens between your agent and Talonic when it reads a file: the four ways a file arrives, the status you can check, and when results are ready to use.

content.text: Your agent sends Talonic a document id, a URL, a local file or an upload link. Talonic reads the file, fills the fields you asked for, and links each value to the page and passage it came from. Values it is unsure about are marked with a lower confidence score so you can check them.
The four ways in and the status to check are on [Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files).

title: Recipe: set up a workspace end to end
seoTitle: Recipe: Set Up a Talonic Workspace from Your AI Agent
description: From an empty workspace to answers: add companies, upload files, choose the fields you want, extract or run a Spec, ask a first question and check credits.

content.text: Go from an empty workspace to structured data and cited answers without opening the web app. For anyone starting with Talonic through an agent.
Connect your agent ([Connect](/docs/mcp/install)). Have a few sample documents ready, for example ten invoices from two suppliers.

"Set up Talonic for our invoices. We buy from Acme GmbH and Nordwind AG; keep their documents apart. I'll upload ten invoices. Pull vendor, invoice number, date, total and currency from each, show me a table, then tell me our total spend per supplier."

items: **Companies.** [`talonic_list_accounts`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-accounts), then [`talonic_create_account`](/docs/mcp/tools/create-account) for each supplier that is missing.

**Files.** [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) per file with `account` and `add_to_workspace: true`; you open each link and drop the file; it checks [`talonic_get_document`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-document) until `completed`.

**Fields.** [`talonic_save_schema`](/docs/mcp/tools/save-schema) with the five fields, so every invoice comes back the same way. (Not sure which fields exist? It can call [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) with `auto_schema: true` on one invoice and show you what it found.)

**Extract.** [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) per document with the saved `schema_id`. If your team already has an invoice Spec, [`talonic_run_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/run-spec) runs it over all ten at once and [`talonic_get_run_results`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-run-results) returns one row each.
**First question.** [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask): "Total spend per supplier", answered with citations to each invoice.
**Check credits.** [`talonic_get_balance`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-balance) and [`talonic_get_usage`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-usage).

content.text: If your role can build processes, ask: "From now on, read every invoice that arrives at invoices@ourcompany.com the same way." The agent drafts it with [`talonic_process_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-create); see [Process an inbox](/docs/mcp/recipes/process-an-inbox).

items: Accounts, schemas, links and look-ups are free. Each document read and each question uses credits.
A Spec run takes up to 500 workspace documents, or 20 public URLs, per call.
Something failing? [Troubleshooting](/docs/mcp/troubleshooting).

title: Recipe: process an inbox
seoTitle: Recipe: Process an Email Inbox with Talonic and an Agent
description: Have every document that arrives in a mailbox read, checked and signed off: describe the process, test it on real files, publish it and work its sign-offs.

content.text: Turn a shared mailbox into a process: every document that arrives is read, checked, sent to the right person to sign when needed, and passed on. For operations and finance teams whose agent can build processes.

items: Your role can see and build processes (the process tools are listed in your session).
The mailbox is connected in the Talonic web app. Connecting a mailbox and storing passwords happen in the web app, never through the agent.

content.text: "Set up a process for ap@ourcompany.com: read each invoice, check the total against the purchase order, have Finance sign anything over 10,000 EUR, and send approved invoices to accounting@ourcompany.com. Test it on last week's invoices before it goes live."

items: **See what's available.** [`talonic_process_setup`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-setup) lists connected mailboxes, who steps can wait for, and the data a look-up step can read.

**Draft.** [`talonic_process_create`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-create) with your description. Nothing runs yet. The answer lists what a person still has to choose (`stillOpen`, `questions`); the agent asks you.
**Adjust.** [`talonic_process_change`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-change) for each answer ("Finance means the Finance group"). If a change means fewer checks, the agent must ask you before it confirms.
**Check.** [`talonic_process_check`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-check) shows what the draft still needs and what publishing would change.

**Test.** [`talonic_process_test_run`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-test-run) on a few real invoices (`document_ids`) in a test copy: nothing is sent. [`talonic_process_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-status) on the test copy shows each item's path.
**Publish.** Only when you say so: [`talonic_process_publish`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-publish) with a `reason`. From now on new mail starts runs.
"What's waiting for me?" → [`talonic_process_waiting_for_me`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-waiting-for-me), then [`talonic_process_status`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-status) to see the items.

"Approve the Acme ones, send the other back: PO number missing." → [`talonic_process_sign`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-sign) with `items`, [`talonic_process_send_back`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-send-back) with a `reason`.

"Anything stuck?" → [`talonic_process_runs`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-runs) with state `stuck`, [`talonic_process_item`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-item) for why, and [`talonic_process_retry`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-retry) once the cause is fixed.
Drafting, checking and reading status are free; each document a run reads uses credits, including test runs.
Signing and sending back are allowed only where you are assigned to the step, exactly as in the web app.
[`talonic_process_rollback`](/docs/mcp/tools/process-rollback) makes an earlier version live again if a change misbehaves.

related.label: Tools by task: build a process

faq.question: Can the agent publish a process on its own?
faq.answer: It can call publish, but it is told to do so only after you say so and after showing you the check. Publishing is checked against your role every time.

title: Recipe: audit invoices
seoTitle: Recipe: Audit Invoices for Duplicates and Outliers — Talonic
description: Ask your agent to audit invoices: find duplicates, totals above a limit and missing fields across the workspace, with every finding linked to its source page.

content.text: Find duplicate invoices, unusually large totals and missing details across everything in your workspace, with each finding linked to the document and page it came from. For finance and audit teams.
Invoices are in the workspace and have been read (by a Spec, a process, or [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract)). [Set up a workspace](/docs/mcp/recipes/set-up-a-workspace) if not.
"Audit our 2026 invoices: any vendor that billed the same amount twice, any invoice over 25,000 EUR, and any without an invoice number. Give me a table with a link to each document."

items: **Duplicates.** [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask): "Which vendors invoiced the same amount more than once in 2026?" The answer cites each pair of invoices.

**Large totals.** [`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data) for "invoice total" to get the field name, then [`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter) with `gt 25000`. Numeric comparisons need a number field; the agent checks first.
**Missing numbers.** [`talonic_filter`](/docs/mcp/tools/filter) with `is_empty` on the invoice-number field.

**Evidence.** For any finding you question, [`talonic_field_values`](/docs/mcp/tools/field-values) or [`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) with `include_provenance` shows the page and passage the value came from.
Every answer comes with citations; open them before acting on a finding.
Values with a confidence below 0.7 are worth a second look.
If a filter returns `warnings[]` (for example a field name it could not match), the agent tells you instead of guessing.
Filters, field values and look-ups are free; each question uses credits.
Results include only documents you are allowed to see.

title: Recipe: answer a contract question
seoTitle: Recipe: Answer a Contract Question with Citations — Talonic
description: Ask what a contract says (notice periods, renewal dates, liability caps) and get an answer that quotes the clause, with a link to the page it comes from.

content.text: Ask what a contract says and get an answer that quotes the clause and links to the page, in one call. For legal, procurement and anyone who needs a term out of a contract quickly.
"What is the notice period for ending our agreement with Acme, and by when do we have to give notice to stop it renewing?"

items: **Find the contract** (optional). [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) with a short keyword ("Acme") to get the `document_id`, so the question looks only at that contract.
**Ask.** [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) with the question and `scope.document_ids`. Talonic answers with citations quoting the clause.
**If it takes longer.** When the answer says `processing`, [`talonic_get_answer`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-answer) with the `ask_id` until it is `completed`.
**Follow up.** "And the liability cap?" goes to [`talonic_ask`](/docs/mcp/tools/ask) again with the same `conversation_id`.
**Read the clause in full** (optional). [`talonic_to_markdown`](/docs/mcp/tools/to-markdown) returns the contract's text.

content.title: Ask about one contract

content.text: The answer's `citations[]` give the quote, the document and a link to open it in the web app. `verification` says whether every claim was backed by a source; if not, `correction` says what changed.

items: Each question uses credits; `usage.credits_charged` on the answer says how many. Search and reading text from a stored document are free.
An answer waits up to 55 seconds (`wait_seconds`) before handing back an `ask_id` to collect later.

faq.question: Can I ask about all contracts at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave out the scope, or scope by `document_type` or tags, and ask "Which of our supplier contracts renew automatically in the next 90 days?".

title: Run Talonic tasks from your own agent
seoTitle: Run Talonic Tasks and Decisions from Your Own Agent: Docs
description: Let your own agent take checks and decisions your workspace hands out: list the work, claim one, read its input, submit a result Talonic checks or hand it back.

content.text: A workspace can hand some work to an outside agent instead of a person: a check a Spec asks for on a document, or a decision an app makes on each run. Your agent picks the work up, does it, and hands back a result that Talonic verifies before anything continues. This page is for teams wiring their own agent into those steps.

items: **Agent tasks** come from a Spec step set to wait for an outside agent. Each has the document's input, instructions and the fields to return. Tools: [`talonic_list_agent_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-agent-tasks), [`talonic_get_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-agent-task), [`talonic_claim_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-agent-task), [`talonic_heartbeat_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-agent-task), [`talonic_submit_agent_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-agent-task).

**Decision tasks** come from an app whose decisions are made outside Talonic. Each has the records to decide on, earlier decisions as precedent, and the shape the decision must take. Tools: [`talonic_list_decision_tasks`](/docs/mcp/tools/list-decision-tasks), [`talonic_claim_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/claim-decision-task), [`talonic_read_decision_package`](/docs/mcp/tools/read-decision-package), [`talonic_heartbeat_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/heartbeat-decision-task), [`talonic_submit_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/submit-decision-task), [`talonic_release_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/release-decision-task), [`talonic_fail_decision_task`](/docs/mcp/tools/fail-decision-task).
**List** available work. (Or subscribe to the webhook your workspace sends when work is offered.)

**Claim** one item. A claim is yours for a limited time (`lease_expires_at`) and carries an `execution_epoch` you send back with every later call. If another agent claimed it first you get HTTP 409; take the next one.
**Read** the input. For decisions, read the records page by page; copy the evidence locators you rely on.
**Keep the claim alive** with a heartbeat if the work takes longer than the lease.

**Submit** the result in exactly the declared shape. Talonic checks it before writing anything; a rejected submission (HTTP 422) says why and changes nothing, so fix it and submit again while the claim lasts.
**Or hand it back.** Release a decision another agent could still make; fail one nobody can decide, which sends it to a person and applies the app's fallback.
Agent tasks: any credential for the workspace; you see only the tasks of that workspace.

Decision tasks: an API key with a `decide` grant for that app, or a connector session with the `apps:decide` scope and a workspace role of senior member or above. A 403 names what is missing (`decide_grant_required`, `insufficient_scope`, `insufficient_tier`); the agent should tell you, not retry.
Every read of a task's input is recorded against the task.

params.description: Someone else holds the claim, or your `execution_epoch` is out of date. Stop, discard the work and list again.
The result does not match the declared shape or evidence. Nothing changed; fix and resubmit.
The credential lacks the grant, scope or role. Reconnect or ask an admin.

content.text: See [Tools by task](/docs/mcp/tools) for the rest of the tools.

faq.question: What happens if my agent crashes in the middle of a task?
faq.answer: The claim runs out at `lease_expires_at` and the task becomes available again. Any later call with the old `execution_epoch` is refused, so stale work can never overwrite a newer result.

title: Troubleshooting
seoTitle: Talonic MCP Troubleshooting: Fix Connection and Tool Errors
description: Fix the common Talonic MCP problems: client won't connect, sign-in loops, authentication errors, missing tools, empty search results and stuck uploads.

content.text: The common problems and their fixes, in the order people hit them. If Talonic is missing from your client's server list, the problem is the connection; if it is listed but a call fails, read the error message first, because it says what to change.

The local server could not read the key. Put it in the `env` block of your client config under exactly `TALONIC_API_KEY`, check the JSON is valid, and fully quit and reopen the client (a new conversation is not enough).
Talonic does not appear in the client

For a local install, `command` must be `npx` and `args` exactly `["-y", "@talonic/mcp@latest"]`. Run `npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest --version` in a terminal: it should print a version. Node.js 18 or later is required.
Connector sign-in does not return to the chat

Sign in at app.talonic.com with the account that owns the workspace, allow third-party cookies for app.talonic.com and your chat client, then start the connector again. With several Talonic accounts, sign out first so the right one is used. Last resort: remove the connector and add `https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp` again.
Every call fails with an authentication error

The key is wrong, revoked or for another workspace. Keys start with `tlnc_`; create a new one under **Settings → API Keys** ([Get an API key](/docs/mcp/api-key)). For connectors, remove and re-add the connector.

Process tools appear only when your role can see processes; app tools only when the app is enabled for you; ChatGPT omits the two generic data-query tools. Decision-task tools marked not callable mean the connector was added before it could ask for `apps:decide`: remove and re-add it. [Tools by task](/docs/mcp/tools) shows what each session lists.
Tool descriptions or tools look out of date
Clients cache the tool list. Restart the client, or reconnect the connector, after Talonic adds or changes tools.
Search returns nothing for something that exists

[`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) matches words literally. Search with one short, singular keyword (`invoice`, not `invoices from May`) or the exact file name. For a concept rather than a word, use [`talonic_find_data`](/docs/mcp/tools/find-data).

Number comparisons work only on fields stored as numbers. Check the field's `dataType` with [`talonic_search`](/docs/mcp/tools/search) or [`talonic_get_field`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-field), and read any `warnings[]` on the response: it names fields it could not match.

[`talonic_extract`](/docs/mcp/tools/extract) needs to know what to pull: an inline `schema`, a saved `schema_id`, or `auto_schema: true` to have Talonic suggest the fields. The error includes a ready-to-use schema for your request.
Extract returns empty fields for a file I attached

In Claude.ai and ChatGPT, a file sent inside the tool call is cut short by the client's size limit. Use [`talonic_request_upload`](/docs/mcp/tools/request-upload) instead ([Files and uploads](/docs/mcp/files)).

`pending_upload` means the link has not been used yet; `uploading`, `queued` and `extracting` are normal while a file is read. `ocr_failed`, `extraction_failed` or `error` are final: try a clearer scan or the original file. An expired link can be replaced by asking for a new one.

Reading time grows with page count. If your client gives up first, use an upload link or a Spec run ([`talonic_run_spec`](/docs/mcp/tools/run-spec)), which return at once and let the agent check progress.
The call runs with your workspace role. The message names what is missing, such as a role, a grant or a scope; ask a workspace admin, or reconnect if it names a scope.

Include your client and its version, the server version (`npx -y @talonic/mcp@latest --version` for local installs), the tool name and the full error message. Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/talonicdev/talonic-mcp/issues) or write to support from the web app.

faq.question: Why does my agent say it can't find a document I know is there?
faq.answer: Search matches words literally. Ask it to search for one short keyword or the exact file name, or to look for the concept instead of the word.

params.description: Page through `talonic_get_run_results` with `cursor`.

params.name: Field values page
params.description: Page through `talonic_field_values` with `cursor`.

params.name: Decision package page
params.description: Page through `talonic_read_decision_package` with `cursor`.

params.name: Usage window
params.description: `talonic_get_usage` defaults to 30 days.

Searching, filtering, listing, looking up and reading stored text are free. [`talonic_get_pricing`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-pricing) has the rates; [`talonic_get_balance`](/docs/mcp/tools/get-balance) the balance.
Done in the web app, not by an agent

items: Connecting a mailbox or another system, and storing passwords or secrets.
Creating API keys and managing members and roles.

title: Upgrading
seoTitle: Upgrading the Talonic MCP Server to the Latest Version
description: Hosted connections always run the latest Talonic MCP server. Local installs update on restart with @latest; pin an exact version when you need repeatable runs.

content.text: Hosted connections (`https://mcp.talonic.com/mcp`) always run the latest version; there is nothing to do except reconnect if your client caches the tool list.

Local installs with `@talonic/mcp@latest` pick up the newest version the next time the client starts. Quit the client fully (not just the conversation) to restart the server. To pin, use an exact version such as `@talonic/mcp@0.1.100`; `npm view @talonic/mcp version` shows the latest.

New versions add tools and optional parameters. Existing parameters and response fields are not removed or renamed without a dated notice in the [changelog](https://github.com/talonicdev/talonic-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
